resources.string: JarvisRider is reading out the caller. Stops when the call is answered or ends.

Hands-free calling for riders. Long-press the power button (or press your Bluetooth headset button) and say \"call Rahul\", \"Rahul ko call karo\", \"redial\" or \"call mom on speaker\". Incoming calls are announced and you can say \"answer\" or \"reject\".
No Bluetooth headset connected right now
Tap \"Digital assistant app\" (or \"Default assist app\") and choose JarvisRider.
Could not open that settings screen on this phone. Please open it manually (see Help).
Android will not ask again for some permissions. Open App info → Permissions and allow them manually.
Auto: English (India) first, Hindi as fallback
Prefer offline speech recognition (needs the offline language pack)

Voice answer/reject needs Android to allow the microphone in the background. It works best when JarvisRider is the default assistant and battery optimization is disabled. If Android blocks it, the caller is still announced and you answer from the headset button.

Not included in this version. An always-listening wake word needs a permanent microphone service, which drains the battery. The free offline engines (Vosk, openWakeWord) would also make the app about 20 times bigger and could not be tested for reliability on real phones yet. Use the power button or the headset button instead.

1. Set JarvisRider as the default digital assistant (Settings → Apps → Default apps → Digital assistant app).\n2. Power button: on Pixel and Android 12+ phones turn on Settings → System → Gestures → \"Press and hold power button\" → Digital assistant. On Samsung the side key can only open Bixby or the power-off menu, so use a long-press of the home button (or swipe up from a bottom corner with gesture navigation) or the headset button.\n3. Bluetooth headset: a long-press of the headset\'s call/multi-function button usually triggers voice dial / assistant. If your headset opens another app, set JarvisRider as default for \"Voice command\" when Android asks.
Disable battery optimization for JarvisRider so Android lets it react to incoming calls. JarvisRider runs nothing in the background while idle, so this costs almost no battery.

• Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO: Security app → Permissions → Autostart → enable JarvisRider. Also App info → Battery saver → No restrictions.
• Oppo / Realme / OnePlus (ColorOS): Settings → Battery → App battery management → JarvisRider → allow background activity and auto launch.
• Vivo / iQOO: i Manager → App manager → Autostart manager → enable JarvisRider; Battery → Background power consumption → allow.
• Samsung: Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → add JarvisRider. Remove it from "Sleeping apps".
Also lock JarvisRider in the recent-apps screen if your phone supports it.

• "Call Rahul" / "Rahul ko call karo" / "राहुल को फ़ोन लगाओ"
• "Call mom on speaker" / "speaker pe papa ko call karo"
• "Redial" / "dobara call karo"
• "Call back" (last call in your log)
• "Call 98765 43210"
• When several contacts match: say "first", "second", "doosra" or the full name.
• "Cancel" / "rehne do" stops.
• Incoming: "answer", "pick up", "haan", "utha lo" / "reject", "cut", "kaat do", "nahi".

• "Speech recognition is not available": install or update the Google app, or download the offline English (India) and Hindi packs (Google app → Settings → Voice → Offline speech recognition).
• Prompts play from the phone instead of the helmet: enable "Use the Bluetooth headset microphone" in Settings and make sure the headset is connected for calls (not only media).
• Assistant not listed: reinstall, then check Settings → Apps → Default apps → Digital assistant app.
• Incoming calls not announced: grant Phone and Call log permissions, disable battery optimization and allow autostart (see above).
Type a name to match, e.g. rahool
TTS failed. Install or enable a text-to-speech engine (Settings → Accessibility → Text-to-speech).
Recognition error code %1$d (6/7 = nothing heard, 2/4 = network/engine, 9 = permission).
